The lighthouse stood at the end of a narrow spit of land, and for most of the year the only visitors were gulls and the occasional surveyor. Its keeper kept a log of the weather, the ships that passed, and the small repairs that a building exposed to salt and wind always needs. In winter the storms came from the north and the waves broke over the lower gallery; in summer the fog rolled in each evening and the horn sounded every thirty seconds until dawn. Over the decades the log filled dozens of volumes. Historians later used it to reconstruct shipping patterns along the coast, because the keeper had noted not only the names of vessels but their cargo, their direction, and how heavily they sat in the water. A bakery in the nearby town still sells a bread named after the lighthouse, although few of its customers know why. The lighthouse stood at the end of a narrow spit of land, and for most of the year the only visitors were gulls and the occasional surveyor. Its keeper kept a log of the weather, the ships that passed, and the small repairs that a building exposed to salt and wind always needs. In winter the storms came from the north and the waves broke over the lower gallery; in summer the fog rolled in each evening and the horn sounded every thirty seconds until dawn. Over the decades the log filled dozens of volumes. Historians later used it to reconstruct shipping patterns along the coast, because the keeper had noted not only the names of vessels but their cargo, their direction, and how heavily they sat in the water. A bakery in the nearby town still sells a bread named after the lighthouse, although few of its customers know why. The recipe calls for rye flour, caraway seeds, a little molasses, and a long, slow rise in a cool kitchen. Engineers who studied the tower found that its foundation had shifted by less than a centimeter in a hundred years, a result they attributed to the careful choice of granite and to drainage channels cut into the rock by the original builders. Modern instruments now measure wind speed, pressure, and visibility automatically, and the data flows to a regional forecasting center where models combine it with satellite images and reports from buoys offshore. The keeper retired long ago, but volunteers still climb the spiral staircase on weekends to polish the brass, wind the old clock, and show children how the great lens concentrates a small flame into a beam visible for twenty nautical miles. Visitors often ask how the lens works. Rings of glass prisms bend the light toward the horizon, so that almost none of it is wasted on the sky or the sea at the foot of the tower. The design was a breakthrough in its day, and variations of it are still used in theater spotlights, overhead projectors, and the headlights of some cars. When the museum opened, the town held a festival with music, a market, and a race along the beach path. The race has become an annual tradition.
